_meta.description: Wallets a U.S. district court ordered forfeited to the United States, read from the Department of Justice official forfeiture notifications. Read by backend/scripts/import_intl_sanctions.py, which files each one under its chain in intl_sanctions*.json as seized.
_meta.provenance: Found by the 11 Nov 2026 sanctions hunt in the USAO official notifications on forfeiture.gov (the current file and Internet Archive copies of earlier ones). Each entry was re-read in that notice on 14 Nov 2026: the address appears inside a notice that the court "entered an Order condemning and forfeiting" the property; court, case, caption and order date are copied from that notice.
_meta.rule: Only a notice of an entered order of forfeiture counts; a complaint or an administrative seizure notice has no outcome yet. Chain is the one the notice names (ETH, AAVE (Ethereum), TRX/USDT on Tron); a 0x wallet the notice puts on another chain is left out. Each 0x address was checked to hold no contract code (keyless RPC, 14 Nov 2026).
_meta.verification_note: A forfeiture order is a court measure against the property, not a sanctions designation and not a finding that anyone who later transacted with the address took part in anything. A holder is named only as the notice names it; an exchange account or bank custody address is the exchange or bank holding the property for that account.
_meta.schema: orders: [{address, chain, holder, court, case, caption, order_entered, notice_url, notice, checked}]
